instrucciones:
Recibes registros de una base de reglas de producción audiovisual con IA. Cada registro trae su texto
literal completo, el documento y la ruta de encabezados donde está, y a veces un contexto (encabezado de tabla o de
bloque). El encabezado dice el alcance: modelo, régimen, etapa, caso. Para CADA registro devuelve:
- "enunciado": la regla en español, UNA frase: qué exige, prohíbe, limita o especifica. Si es un ejemplo o una
  explicación sin norma, empieza con "Ejemplo:" o "Explicación:".
- "alcance": a qué aplica exactamente según texto y encabezado (modelo y versión, caso, etapa, régimen) o "general".
- "temas": de 1 a 3 claves de la lista, las que mejor describen de qué trata.
Lista de temas (clave: descripción):
marca_brandlock: brand-lock: secciones, paleta hex, tipografía, never list, voz, confianza de valores
estrategia_conceptos: brief, SMP, territorios, concept cards, matriz, dirección narrativa
guion_formato: guion: sluglines, acción, personajes, diálogo, XML, estructura, escenas
dramaturgia_escena: fórmula de escena, three-jobs, blocking, staging, poder, geometría, mirada
tres_detalles: ley de los tres detalles: presión ambiental, micro-acción, motivo sonoro/visual
emocion_sin_nombrar: mostrar no contar, emoción como cuerpo u objeto, 2-4 señales
vocabulario_prohibido: palabras vetadas, anti-slop, cinematic/epic/masterpiece, adjetivos vacíos
cinco_anclas_motivo: cinco anclas, objeto ancla, motivo, imagen final, quiebre

Devuelve JSON {"registros": [{"id": "...", "enunciado": "...", "alcance": "...", "temas": ["..."]}]} con
exactamente los ids recibidos, en el mismo orden.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Beat Frameworks › Custom

registros.texto:
If the brief doesn't fit, build a custom beat structure. Document in `storyboard.md`:

```markdown
## Beat framework: Custom

**Why custom:** [one sentence, what made the standard frameworks insufficient]

**Beats:**
1. [name], [purpose], [duration]
2. ...
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Beat Frameworks › Custom

registros.texto: Custom is a last resort, not a first move. The standard frameworks exist because they work.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text

registros.texto: Text on screen is a load-bearing decision. Most storyboards over-text. The default should be: **does this shot need text to land?** If the visual carries the meaning, text dilutes.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › When on-screen text earns its keep

registros.texto: 1. **Auto-play-mute environments.** Social feeds. Text replaces VO.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › When on-screen text earns its keep

registros.texto: 2. **Concept compression.** A short phrase lands harder than 4 seconds of narration.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › When on-screen text earns its keep

registros.texto: 3. **Stat or proof point.** Numbers stick visually in a way they don't audibly.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › When on-screen text earns its keep

registros.texto: 4. **Beat punctuation.** A single word or phrase that lands on a music hit.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › When on-screen text earns its keep

registros.texto: 5. **CTA.** The action you want the viewer to take.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › When on-screen text doesn't earn its keep

registros.texto: 1. **Restating the VO.** If the voice says it, the text is noise.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › When on-screen text doesn't earn its keep

registros.texto: 2. **Decorative copy.** "Moments matter" floating over b-roll. Cut it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › When on-screen text doesn't earn its keep

registros.texto: 3. **Brand vibing.** Product names everywhere. Logo lockup in the CTA covers this.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › When on-screen text doesn't earn its keep

registros.texto: 4. **Filler beats.** If the shot doesn't need text, leave it clean.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules

registros.texto: These flow into the `position` field of each text overlay.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Negative-space-aware composition

registros.texto: When a shot has on-screen text, the **shot subject must reserve space for it**. This is enforced at storyboard time, not generation time.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Negative-space-aware composition

registros.texto:
If text is in the right third → subject composition leaves the right third clear.
If text is lower third → subject upper two-thirds.
If text is centered → subject framed to negative space around center.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Negative-space-aware composition

registros.texto: This goes into the shot's rationale: "MCU left-third subject, reserves right-third for `text_03`."

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Positions

registros.texto: | `center` | Display headline, single concept, hard cut in/out |

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Positions

registros.texto: | `lower-third` | Caption / VO substitute, persistent across shots |

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Positions

registros.texto: | `upper-third` | Stat callout, secondary information |

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Positions

registros.texto: | `left-third` | Subject is right-weighted in frame |

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Positions

registros.texto: | `right-third` | Subject is left-weighted in frame |

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Positions

registros.texto: | `{x: %, y: %}` | Custom, only when the standard positions don't fit |

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Sizes

registros.texto: | `display` | 96–144 px | Hero/hook beats |

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Sizes

registros.texto: | `headline` | 56–80 px | Reframe beats |

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Sizes

registros.texto: | `body` | 32–48 px | Caption-style, persistent |

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Sizes

registros.texto: | `caption` | 20–28 px | Disclaimers, attribution |

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Animation

registros.texto:
Default to clean, not flashy:

- Hook beats → `hard-cut` in, `hard-cut` out (no fade)
- Reframe beats → `fade-in` 0.2s, `fade-out` 0.2s
- Persistent captions → `slide-up` in, `slide-down` out
- CTA → `type-on` for a typewriter effect, or `slide-up`

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Animation

registros.texto: Avoid stacking animations. Pick one per overlay.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Color rules

registros.texto: The `color` field of every text overlay must be a hex value that exists in the brand-lock palette. If you find yourself wanting a color that's not in the palette, the answer is not to add it, the answer is to pick a different overlay style or shot composition.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Typography rules

registros.texto: Same: every `font` field must reference a font defined in brand-lock typography. Two fonts max per project (display + body). More than that and the brand stops being recognizable.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › The "read twice" rule

registros.texto: Already covered in timing-rules.md but worth repeating: text needs to be on screen long enough for someone to read it twice. Calculate, then verify. Don't eyeball.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Stacking text across shots

registros.texto:
Text can persist across consecutive shots. This is useful when:

- The text takes longer to read than a single shot's duration
- You want text to feel anchored while visuals change underneath

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Stacking text across shots

registros.texto: To stack, both shots reference the same `on_screen_text` ID. The overlay's `enter.at` aligns to the first shot's start, `exit.at` aligns to the second shot's end.

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Stacking text across shots

registros.texto:
In `shots.json`:

```json
{ "id": "shot_03", "on_screen_text": "text_02", ... },
{ "id": "shot_04", "on_screen_text": "text_02", ... }
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Stacking text across shots

registros.texto:
In `text-overlays.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "text_02",
  "shot_id": ["shot_03", "shot_04"],
  ...
}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: On-Screen Text › Stacking text across shots

registros.texto: Document this in rationale: "text persists across shot 3-4 to give 4.8s read-time for 16-word reframe."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar

registros.texto: Controlled vocabulary. Use these exact terms in `shots.json`. Generators interpret loose language inconsistently, locked vocabulary survives translation.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Framing (subject size in frame)

registros.texto: | `ECU` | Extreme close-up | Eyes, hands, single detail |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Framing (subject size in frame)

registros.texto: | `CU` | Close-up | Head, or full hand-on-object |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Framing (subject size in frame)

registros.texto: | `MCU` | Medium close-up | Head and shoulders |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Framing (subject size in frame)

registros.texto: | `MS` | Medium shot | Waist up |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Framing (subject size in frame)

registros.texto: | `MLS` | Medium long shot | Full body, environment minimal |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Framing (subject size in frame)

registros.texto: | `WS` | Wide shot | Full body, environment present |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Framing (subject size in frame)

registros.texto: | `EWS` | Extreme wide shot | Subject small in environment |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Framing (subject size in frame)

registros.texto: Default to MCU and MS for talking-head founder content. ECU and CU for product detail and emotion. WS and EWS for context-setting.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Angle (camera vertical position)

registros.texto: | `eye-level` | Neutral, default |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Angle (camera vertical position)

registros.texto: | `high` | Subject feels smaller, vulnerable |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Angle (camera vertical position)

registros.texto: | `low` | Subject feels powerful, dominant |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Angle (camera vertical position)

registros.texto: | `overhead` | Detached, schematic, instructional |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Angle (camera vertical position)

registros.texto: | `dutch` | Tilted, tension, unease |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Angle (camera vertical position)

registros.texto: Default to eye-level. Use the others deliberately, not for variety.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Motion (camera movement)

registros.texto: | `static` | No movement | Default. Static is not boring. |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Motion (camera movement)

registros.texto: | `push` | Camera moves toward subject | Building intensity, revealing |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Motion (camera movement)

registros.texto: | `pull` | Camera moves away | Releasing, contextualizing |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Motion (camera movement)

registros.texto: | `pan-left` / `pan-right` | Camera rotates horizontally | Surveying environment |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Motion (camera movement)

registros.texto: | `tilt-up` / `tilt-down` | Camera rotates vertically | Reveal scale or detail |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Motion (camera movement)

registros.texto: | `handheld` | Subtle organic shake | Documentary feel, urgency |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Motion (camera movement)

registros.texto: | `orbit` | Camera circles subject | Hero shots, product reveal |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Motion (camera movement)

registros.texto: | `whip` | Fast pan as transition | Beat-cuts in fast-paced content |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Motion (camera movement)

registros.texto: For AI-generated still frames, motion is mostly intent for the editor. For motion-video prompts (Kling, Veo, Seedance, Hailuo), motion translates directly.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Depth of field

registros.texto: | `shallow` | Subject sharp, background blurred |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Depth of field

registros.texto: | `deep` | Everything in focus |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Depth of field

registros.texto: | `rack` | Focus shifts mid-shot |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Depth of field

registros.texto: Default to shallow for talking-head, deep for environmental and schematic.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Lighting style (referenced from series_lock)

registros.texto:
Don't redefine per shot. Define once in `series_lock.lighting`. Examples:

- `soft natural side-light, large window left, warm afternoon`
- `hard top-light, single source, deep shadows, studio black`
- `practical mixed sources, neon accents, urban night`

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Lighting style (referenced from series_lock)

registros.texto: The series_lock string flows into every prompt automatically.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Subject description

registros.texto:
Structured, not poetic. Pattern:

```
[who/what], [doing what], [emotional or compositional note]
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Subject description

registros.texto:
Good:
```
"Founder, mid-thirties, leaning forward at laptop, face partially turned to window light"
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Subject description

registros.texto:
Bad:
```
"A determined entrepreneur conquering the digital frontier with passion"
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › Subject description

registros.texto: Generators reward precision. Adjectives describing emotion ("determined", "passionate") produce stock-photo aesthetics. Describe what the camera actually sees.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › What goes in `subject` vs `series_lock` vs `brand_lock`

registros.texto:
This trips people up. The rule:

- **brand_lock**, locked across the entire project. Palette, type, "never" list.
- **series_lock**, locked across this storyboard. Character anchor, environment, lighting style, color grade.
- **subject (per shot)**, what's different about *this* shot. Action, expression, framing-specific composition notes.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Shot Grammar › What goes in `subject` vs `series_lock` vs `brand_lock`

registros.texto: If you find yourself repeating the same lighting description across shots, it belongs in series_lock. If you find yourself repeating the same color description across storyboards, it belongs in brand_lock.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules

registros.texto: Pacing is math, not feel. Use these as defaults. Override only with reason documented in rationale.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › Shot duration baselines

registros.texto: If a single shot is longer than 7 seconds in a 30-second piece, justify it in rationale. Long shots are not bad. Unjustified long shots are.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › Hook timing (the first beat)

registros.texto:
The hook is 0–2s. Always. There are no exceptions in short-form content. Specifically:

- 9:16 social: first frame must telegraph the topic. Auto-play on mute means the first half-second is fighting a swipe.
- 16:9 in-feed: first 2s decides watch-time.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › Hook timing (the first beat)

registros.texto: The hook shot framing should be high-contrast against the shots that follow. If shot 2 is MS, shot 1 should not be MS. Visual contrast = retention.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › CTA timing (the final beat)

registros.texto:
The CTA is the final 4–6s for 30s content, 6–10s for 60s content. Specifically:

- Last shot should hold long enough for someone to read the CTA text and act
- Don't put motion on the CTA shot, let the text breathe
- If there's a logo lockup, it lives in the final 2s, not earlier

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › On-screen text duration math

registros.texto: A text overlay needs to be on screen long enough to be **read twice**. Not once, twice. Why: viewers are skimming, eyes don't always lock on first frame.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › On-screen text duration math

registros.texto:
Reading speed reference (assume average viewer):
- 1 short word (≤5 chars): 0.6s minimum read
- Short phrase (≤6 words): 1.2s
- Sentence (≤14 words): 2.4s
- Long sentence (15–25 words): 4.0s

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › On-screen text duration math

registros.texto: Multiply by 2 for the "read twice" rule. So a 6-word phrase needs **2.4s on screen minimum**.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › On-screen text duration math

registros.texto:
If a shot is 2 seconds and you need a 14-word sentence, you have a problem. Either:
1. Shorten the copy
2. Carry the text across two consecutive shots (text persists during cut)
3. Lengthen the shot

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › On-screen text duration math

registros.texto: Do not under-time text. It's the most common storyboard failure.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › Pacing curve
Timing Rules › Pacing curve

registros.texto: The apex is two-thirds in, not at the end. The CTA is a release, not a peak.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › Pacing curve

registros.texto: For 60-second content, scale the same curve. Apex around 0:40, CTA from 0:50.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Timing Rules › Validating timing

registros.texto:
Before declaring done, check:

1. Sum of `(end - start)` across all shots equals project duration ±0.1s
2. No shot has `start >= end`
3. No two shots overlap
4. First shot starts at 0.0
5. Last shot ends at project duration
6. Every text overlay's `enter.at` is ≥ its shot's `start`
7. Every text overlay's `exit.at` is ≤ its shot's `end` (or carries to a flagged successor shot)
8. Every text overlay's on-screen duration ≥ read-twice threshold

ubicaciones.encabezado: frontmatter › description

registros.texto: description: Render a structured storyboard (storyboard.md, shots.json, text-overlays.json, brand-lock.snapshot.md) into a single-file HTML preview that is shareable, printable, and offline. Use when the user wants to share a storyboard, export for review, hand off to an editor, or print a hard copy. Triggers on "preview the storyboard", "share this", "export to HTML", "print version", or after a storyboard-architect run. Produces one self-contained .html file with no build or server.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview

registros.texto: You are turning structured storyboard files into a single shareable HTML document. The output is what an editor, stakeholder, or client opens in a browser without thinking about it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview

registros.texto: The constraint is non-negotiable: **single file, no build step, no server, works offline.** Any time the output requires "run this build command" or "host this somewhere," the skill has failed.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › When to use

registros.texto:
Trigger when the user:

- Asks to preview, share, or export a storyboard
- Wants a printable version
- Says "what's the next step" after a storyboard-architect run
- Hands off `storyboard.md` + `shots.json` + asks for a deliverable for review

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › What you produce

registros.texto: One file: `preview.html`. Self-contained. Inline CSS. No JavaScript dependencies (vanilla JS only, embedded). No external font files (uses system stack with brand-font fallbacks). No external images (placeholder slots; if generated images exist, embed as base64 OR reference relative paths).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › What you produce

registros.texto:
```
output/
├── run.json                   # input, for the run id and date
├── storyboard.md              # input
├── shots.json                 # input
├── text-overlays.json         # input
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › What you produce

registros.texto:
If the user has generated frames, the HTML references them via relative paths so the file
works when the whole `output/` folder is shared. Resolve a shot's frame in this order:

1. An entry in `shot.assets.generated` marked `accepted: true`
2. The newest entry in `shot.assets.generated`
3. `frames/round-{highest}/{shot_id}.{png,jpg,jpeg,webp}`
4. `generated/{shot_id}.{ext}`, the pre-3.0.0 flat layout

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › What you produce

registros.texto:
Data first, convention second. Reading the path convention first meant the page showed
whatever file happened to sit there, accepted or rejected, first draft or fifth re-roll.

registros.texto:

Required:

Optional:

registros.texto:
Validate before rendering, and stop if it fails:

```bash
python tools/validate_shots.py output/
```

registros.texto:
From `brand-lock.snapshot.md`, extract:

- Palette (hex values), used for HTML accent colors
- Display font and body font names, used as font-family values with system fallbacks
- Brand voice / mood, used in subtle copy choices

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 2. Extract brand parameters

registros.texto: The HTML preview should *feel* like the brand without going overboard. Quiet branding, not loud.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 3. Generate the HTML

registros.texto: Use `templates/preview.html.tpl` as the structural template. Read it before generating.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 3. Generate the HTML

registros.texto:
The HTML structure: ``` {project title}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto: Resolve each shot's frame by the order in "What you produce" above, then reference it by a path relative to the output root: ```html ```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto: This works when the whole output folder is zipped and shared.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto:
For hard-copy print (a single file with no folder structure), the skill can offer to inline
frames as base64. Ask the user which they prefer if frames are present.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto:
If a shot's `assets.generated` entry carries a `sha256` and the file no longer matches it,
render the frame but say so on the page. That mismatch means the frame changed after it was
recorded, which is exactly the case where a preview quietly showing the new file is worse
than one that flags it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto:
If no frames exist, render styled placeholder cards showing the framing, subject, and shot
spec. These are still useful for stakeholder review at the storyboard stage.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto:
**Template flag convention.** When composing the per-shot context for `preview.html.tpl`, set exactly one of:

- `has_image: true` and `image_path: "frames/round-2/shot_NN.png"`, when a frame exists
- `has_no_image: true`, when none does (renders the placeholder card)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto: The template uses two parallel `{{#if}}` blocks rather than `{{#if}}/{{else}}` to keep the rendering portable across template engines.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto:
For text overlays, set `has_overlays: true` and an `overlays` array on the shot. Each entry
carries `id`, `content`, `font`, `weight`, `color`, `size`, `position_class`,
`position_label`, `enter_at`, `enter_animation`, `exit_at`, `exit_animation`. The template
iterates that array with `{{#each overlays}}`.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto:
It is an array because `shots.json` lets a shot carry several overlays and
`text-overlays.json` always did. A single set of `overlay_*` fields could hold one, so the
second overlay on a shot rendered nowhere and nothing reported it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto:
For verdict badges, set `has_verdict`, `verdict`, `verdict_round`, and `verdict_class`
(the lowercased verdict) from the newest critique for that shot under `critiques/`. Omit
them when the shot has no critique.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 4. Embed frames if available

registros.texto:
**Escape everything.** Subjects, rationales, VO lines, and overlay copy are model-generated
prose that lands in both text and attribute contexts. One angle bracket in a rationale, or
one quote in an overlay font name, breaks the page a client is reading.
`tools/shots-to-html.py` escapes every substitution by default and reserves raw output for
the inlined CSS alone.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 5. Render text overlays visually

registros.texto:
For every shot with an `on_screen_text` reference, the HTML shows:

- The text content rendered in approximately the brand font (or visible fallback)
- The position indicated visually (lower-third, center, etc.)
- Timing info (enter/exit beats)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 5. Render text overlays visually

registros.texto: This gives the reviewer a sense of what the final composited frame will look like, even before final compositing happens.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 6. Print stylesheet

registros.texto:
Include `@media print` rules that:

- Hide nav, footer scripts, expand/collapse UI
- Force one shot per page (or two if compact)
- Ensure text overlays render legibly
- Use black-on-white where brand colors won't print well

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Workflow › Step 6. Print stylesheet

registros.texto: The user should be able to hit Cmd-P / Ctrl-P and get a clean PDF.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Hard rules › Rule 1. Single file, no exceptions

registros.texto: The output is one `.html` file. If you find yourself wanting a separate stylesheet or JS file, inline it. If you find yourself wanting a build step, you're solving the wrong problem.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Hard rules › Rule 2. No external dependencies at runtime

registros.texto: No CDN scripts. No Google Fonts. No external CSS frameworks. The file must work with no internet connection.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Hard rules › Rule 2. No external dependencies at runtime

registros.texto: The exception: if the user explicitly opts in (e.g. "make it pretty, I'm online"), Tailwind via CDN is acceptable. Default is no.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Hard rules › Rule 3. Print must work

registros.texto: Hit Cmd-P. The result should be a clean PDF. If layout breaks across page boundaries, the print stylesheet is broken.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Hard rules › Rule 4. Brand-aware but quiet

registros.texto: Use brand colors as accents, not as full backgrounds. The reviewer's job is to read the storyboard, not admire the design. Subtle.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Hard rules › Rule 5. Mobile-readable

registros.texto: Stakeholders open links on phones. The HTML should be readable on mobile without horizontal scroll. Simple responsive CSS.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Templates

registros.texto:
- `templates/preview.html.tpl`, the structural template
- `templates/styles.css.tpl`, the CSS to inline
- `templates/print.css.tpl`, the print rules

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Templates

registros.texto: The skill reads all three and assembles them into a single `preview.html`.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Quality bar

registros.texto:
Before declaring done, verify:

- [ ] File opens in any browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) with no errors
- [ ] No external network requests fire on load
- [ ] Print preview produces a clean PDF
- [ ] Mobile viewport (375px) renders without horizontal scroll
- [ ] Brand colors and fonts come from the brand-lock, not from a fallback
- [ ] Every shot from `shots.json` is present
- [ ] Every overlay referenced by a shot is rendered, including second and third overlays
- [ ] `brand_lock_ref` from `shots.json` is what the footer links to, not a hardcoded name
- [ ] The run date and the render date are both shown, and labelled differently
- [ ] No `{{` remains anywhere in the output

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Quality bar

registros.texto:
The CLI renderer checks the mechanical half of that list against itself:

```bash
python tools/shots-to-html.py --selftest
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Two timestamps, not one

registros.texto:
"Run" is when the storyboard was produced, read from `run.json`. "Rendered" is when the page
was written. They are separate lines in the footer and they must stay separate.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Two timestamps, not one

registros.texto:
Collapsing them into a single "Generated" date meant re-rendering a preview six months later
restamped the run as today, and the footer went on asserting the page was built against a
brand-lock on a date that had nothing to do with the frames above it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard HTML Preview › Two timestamps, not one

registros.texto:
If the brand-lock on disk no longer hashes to what `run.json` recorded, say so on the page.
The reader is looking at frames built against a brand state they can no longer see.

ubicaciones.encabezado: frontmatter › description

registros.texto: description: Use this skill whenever the user asks to create, improve, audit, or split prompts for AI video generators (Seedance, Kling, Veo, Runway, Luma, Pika, Sora, any image-to-video system). The skill also covers storyboards, shot lists, director treatments, dynamic montage, multi-clip story structure, camera direction, lighting, blocking, pacing, character continuity, dialogue, and sound design. Trigger even when the user says things like "придумай сцену для видео", "разбей на склейки", "сделай раскадровку", "улучши промпт для Kling", "переведи сценарий в промпты", "как снять X в AI-видео", or shares a prompt and asks to fix it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: AI Director, Screenwriter & Editor

registros.texto: Hybrid role. You direct (see frame, emotion, motivated camera), write (build beat, action, consequence, final image), and edit (cut rhythm, protect continuity, drive montage). Prompt engineering is fourth — it serves the first three.

ubicaciones.encabezado: AI Director, Screenwriter & Editor

registros.texto: A beautiful frame without dramaturgy is wallpaper. A dramaturgically clean prompt without details is mush. The whole craft of this skill lives in the reference files. The body of this SKILL.md is intentionally thin so you cannot fake a result by reading it alone.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Mandatory reading order — DO NOT WRITE A PROMPT WITHOUT THIS

registros.texto: Past attempts to write prompts directly from this skill body produced lazy, mush-prone results. The fix is structural: the process lives only in the reference files, and you load them in this order before producing output. Skipping a step **silently** degrades the result — the model cannot tell that a shot is wallpaper, only the writer can, and only by applying the rules from these files.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Mandatory reading order — DO NOT WRITE A PROMPT WITHOUT THIS › Step 3 — pick the model and read **one** model file

registros.texto:
Default if nothing in the request hints at a model:
- Multi-shot narrative or fast montage drama → Seedance, or Kling 3.0 if dialogue is involved.
- Dialogue / commercial polish / synchronized SFX → Veo, or Kling 3.0 for multi-character dialogue scenes up to 15s.
- Character consistency across many social clips → Kling 2.6 Pro (cheaper) or Kling 3.0 (with in-prompt `[Character A: ...]` labels).
- 10-15s continuous narrative with audio → Kling 3.0.
- 15-30s continuous single-generation arc, heavy reference kits (up to 50 assets), editing or extending existing footage, 30-180s long-form → Seedance 2.5.
- Face-heavy drama → Seedance 2.5 (realistic humans + lip-sync are its headline feature), Kling, or Veo. On a 2.0-only pipeline route faces to 1.5 Pro (2.0 filters human faces aggressively).
